newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-ENQVIST SETS UP SWEDISH TIE WITH SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ENQVIST SETS UP SWEDISH TIE WITH SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: Sweden won both reverse singles to crush Switzerland 4-1 in their Davis Cup world group first round tie on Sunday and book a quarter-final against South Africa in April.
Sweden started the day leading 2-1 and victory was assured when world number 10 Thomas Enqvist beat a tired Marc Rosset 6-3 6-2 3-6 6-2.
In the last dead-rubber match Magnus Larsson beat Ivo Heuberger, a last-minute replacement for Lorenzo Manta, 3-6 6-4 6-2.

Sweden, runners-up in the 1996 Davis Cup when they lost 3-2 to France in the final in Malmo just nine weeks ago, were hot favourites and warmed the home crowd in this city near the Arctic Circle despite the freezing temperatures.
Sweden's captain Carl-Axel Hageskog vowed to take the team all the way despite the marked absence of Swedish Davis Cup champion Stefan Edberg, who retired last year.
"We are eager to bring the Cup to Sweden. With the team spirit and the very good players I have, I think it's possible," he said. "We have to go for it."

The first day had ended level after Enqvist, the Swedish number one, and Rosset, 24th in the world, had both won their opening singles. Sweden then took the advantage on Saturday with a five-set marathon win for their doubles team of Nicklas Kulti and Mikael Tillstrom.
The key match was always going to be Enqvist-Rosset. The Swede took early control and Rosset suffered through some inconsistent serving and shaky temperament.
His temper matched his bright orange shoes and he lost control in the fourth set, breaking his racket after slamming it into the court on the way to dropping the set 6-2 to hand the tie to Sweden.
Rosset said his five-set victory over Larsson on Friday coupled with Saturday's doubles loss had taken its toll.
"I played like a guy who had played 10 sets before," said Rosset whose service, so excellent in his opening match, proved his Achilles heel. His 15 aces were offset by six double faults.
Enqvist said he felt like he was in control from the start.
"He played a good third set but I was on top of him the whole time. He was a bit tired and I made him run," he said.
